s01.narration: Want every colleague to know right away who their manager is? Hi, I'm Maria from the Sloneek team, and I'll show you how to create an org chart.

s02.narration: You'll find the org chart in the left menu, in the Company section, under Teams.

s03.narration: I click Teams, and the Teams and organizational structure page opens.

s04.narration: Each box is one team: people with a role in the team are at the top, members are below the line, and their positions are in brackets.

s05.narration: If you turn off Show users, you'll see just the company's skeleton, meaning which teams belong under which.

s06.narration: Where a team sits is set by its Parent team field, and a team without one stands on its own, like Customer Support here.

s07.narration: I turn users back on and click Add to open the Create a team form.

s08.narration: In the Name field, I type the name of the new team, Technical Support.

s09.narration: In the description, I write what the team does, and anyone who clicks on the team can read it.

s10.narration: In the Parent team field, I choose Customer Support, so the new team goes under it.

s11.narration: As the manager, I choose James Miller, who will approve the team's absences.

s12.narration: In the Team members field, I add my colleague Olivia Brown.

s13.narration: Further down are other roles, such as a supervisor who only follows what's going on in the team, or attendance and absence approvers.

s14.narration: If a team has no manager, its members' approval requests go to all administrators.

s15.narration: I click Save, and an arrow appears under Customer Support, with the new team tucked beneath it.

s16.narration: I expand the branch with the arrow, and Technical Support sits under Customer Support.

s17.narration: James and Olivia aren't shown yet, because by default the chart only shows active users.

s18.narration: If you turn off Show only active, you'll also see inactive people with a red dot, such as new hires before their start date.

s19.narration: James has a manager icon next to his name, and Olivia is below the line as a team member, along with her position.

s20.narration: The toggle at the top rotates the chart, so the branches spread out from left to right.

s21.narration: I switch back to the original view, and with the Show positions checkbox, you can then hide the positions in brackets.

s22.narration: With the buttons on the right, you collapse or expand the branches, and with Download PNG, you save the chart as an image.

s23.narration: Clicking the team name opens its detail with the description, manager and members.

s24.narration: With the pencil button, you can edit the team at any time, and if you change the parent team, the chart rearranges itself.

s25.narration: I close the form without changes and click on Olivia to see her position and contact details.

s26.narration: Through her name, I go to the user profile, where the Position field sets what appears in brackets in the chart.

s27.narration: The Team field shows where Olivia belongs, and each user can be a member of only one team but can have roles in several teams.

s28.narration: You add new positions through the Manage positions link, which leads to the Positions and competencies section.

s29.narration: In the left menu, I click Teams again, and I'm back at the chart.

s291.narration: I click Switch to the table, and you'll see teams and people as a list.

s30.narration: Here you can move people and whole teams between teams by dragging the handle on the left.

s31.narration: The Switch to the tree button takes you back to the chart.

s32.narration: Who can see the chart is set elsewhere, so in the left menu, I click Settings.

s321.narration: In the expanded menu, I open Application settings and find the option for the team structure.

s322.narration: The Show team structure to all users option decides whether employees can see the chart too.

s33.narration: Employees then only view the chart and find their manager right away, while the administrator sets up teams and roles.

s34.narration: Everyone can find their colleagues' contact details on the Colleagues page, right above Teams.

s35.narration: Now you know how to create a team, place it in the chart and give it a manager and members, and if something doesn't work, check the Help Center.

s36.narration: Less admin, more time for people. This is Sloneek.
